claims.claim: Copyright protects eligible original works of authorship fixed in a tangible medium, but not ideas, methods, systems, or processes as such.
A trademark identifies the source of goods or services and distinguishes them from competitors; it is not ownership of a word or phrase in the abstract.
USPTO guidance describes a U.S. patent as a time-limited right to exclude specified acts involving a qualifying invention, rather than a general affirmative right to make or sell.
USPTO trade-secret policy identifies independent economic value from secrecy, inability to ascertain through proper means, and reasonable secrecy efforts as required high-level elements.

Patent and trade-secret frameworks differ materially because patents involve public disclosure and limited duration, while trade-secret treatment depends on continuing secrecy and does not have a fixed term if its elements persist.
A brand is a broader marketing concept, while a trademark is a source-identifying sign; a real-world asset may raise more than one IP question.
The four-category framework cannot determine rights, ownership, eligibility, infringement, or strategy for a specific asset because legal results depend on jurisdiction and facts.

sourceRecords.notes: Official overview read for original works, fixation, the idea-expression boundary, and the high-level exclusive-rights context. Used only for original synthesis; no Copyright Office prose was adapted.

sourceRecords.title: What Does Copyright Protect? (FAQ)
sourceRecords.notes: Official FAQ read to verify that copyright protects original authorship rather than ideas, concepts, systems, or methods, and that names, titles, slogans, and short phrases are not covered by copyright. Used in original prose only.

sourceRecords.title: What is a trademark?
sourceRecords.notes: Official USPTO explanation read for trademark source identification, goods/services distinction, and the limit that a trademark is not ownership of a word or phrase in general. No filing guidance is drawn from it.

sourceRecords.title: Trademark, patent, or copyright
sourceRecords.notes: Official comparison read for the basic distinction among trademarks, patents, copyrights, and the USPTO's brand-versus-trademark explanation. Used for a high-level comparison only.

sourceRecords.title: Patent essentials
sourceRecords.notes: Official patent overview read for the limited right-to-exclude concept, public disclosure, U.S. territorial framing, broad patent categories, and the boundary that abstract ideas alone are not patentable. The lesson does not assess eligibility or provide patent steps.

sourceRecords.title: Trade secret policy
sourceRecords.notes: Official policy overview read for the three stated trade-secret elements, the dependence on reasonable secrecy efforts, no fixed duration if the elements continue, and the conceptual comparison with patents. Used as a high-level description only.
